member.name: T:Bezoro.Chess.Networking.AuthoritativeChessMatch
member.summary: A small transport-independent command boundary around a private, locally validated chess match.
member.remarks: The host authenticates each connection and maps it to a seat; never accept a seat supplied by the client as proof of identity. Public operations serialize state access. Only the configured engine seat may receive engine moves. No sockets, polling loop, tasks, or engine processes are created during local play.

member.summary: Creates and validates a match. Takebacks are opt-in; the default history budget is 4096 halfmoves.

Starting position and complete saved move history.
Optional authoritative clocks.
Whether both players may agree to restore previous positions, including after a result.
Optional computer-controlled seat; peer commands cannot impersonate it.
Host resource limit for the complete retained move history.
Optional clock source; use a monotonic elapsed-time source for server clocks.

member.name: M:Bezoro.Chess.Networking.AuthoritativeChessMatch.Submit(Bezoro.Chess.Networking.ChessPlayerSeat,Bezoro.Chess.Networking.ChessMatchCommand)
member.summary: Validates an authenticated player's action against the current authoritative revision.
member.remarks: Only accepted commands consume a sequence. Start at one and increment by one after acceptance. The last accepted command and receipt per seat are retained for bounded idempotent redelivery; older requests are rejected. A duplicate receipt can have an older revision than a subsequently received snapshot; clients must keep their newest revision.

member.summary: Restores halfmoves in an opted-in casual engine game and invalidates an outstanding engine reply.
member.remarks: This is a host operation. Authenticate and authorize a human request before calling it. Two-player games require the takeback command/consent flow instead.

member.summary: Requests one engine move outside the state lock, applying it only if its captured revision remains current.
member.remarks: Call on the authoritative host using its own finite search budget. At most one engine request may be outstanding.
